::: {.callout-note}
## The brief: reference policies (emerging folder)

> *"Twenty 2025 emerging-market policies taken from the test files (same columns, plus line). For each one, show in
> your written report how you build the office premium from your predicted risk premium using the expenses
> assumptions. This is assessed by the judging panel and does not affect the Kaggle score."*

This page does that build-up live for each of the 20 policies: the **risk premium** (the model's expected claim cost
for 2025, per policy-year, in competition currency units, CU) and the **office premium** (what the customer is
charged once expenses, commission, tax, reinsurance and profit are added).
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## How to use the calculator

1. **Pick a reference policy** in the menu below. Each entry shows its number (0 to 19), its type letter in brackets
   (**[M]** motor, **[C]** contents, **[B]** buildings), its row ID and its policy ID.
2. The row ID picks the calculator: **M = motor, C = home contents, B = home buildings**. All three calculators are
   shown side by side; the one in use is highlighted and the other two are greyed out at zero.
3. Each calculator shows the build-up from **risk premium to office premium**, line by line, using the emerging-market
   expense assumptions in the table below.
4. **Change any rating factor** further down to see the risk and office premiums move.
5. The table at the bottom prices all 20 reference policies side by side.

**Limitation, home buildings:** Gerard's buildings model has two parts. The **large-claim part is a GLM** and is
calculated here. The **small-claim part is XGBoost** (gradient boosting), which this page can't run, so for buildings
the full risk premium and the office premium are shown as **not possible (XGBoost)**. The GLM large-claim part is
shown on its own so you can still see how the buildings rating factors move it.
:::

```{ojs}
import {scorePolicy, splineValue, officePremium, PROPERTY_LINES} from "./glm.js"
```

${currentCase.partial ? html`<div class="callout callout-style-default callout-warning"><div class="callout-body"><p><strong>Limitation:</strong> the buildings small-claim model is XGBoost, so the full risk premium and the office premium are <strong>not possible</strong> here. Only the <strong>large-claim GLM part</strong> is calculated.</p></div></div>` : ""}`

## Risk premium to office premium

```{ojs}
// only a complete risk premium gets an office premium (not buildings: its XGBoost part is missing)
officeNow = result && !result.incomplete ? officePremium(result.final, line, currentCase.channel, rates) : null
```

```{ojs}
function calcPanel(l) {
  const active = l === line
  const o = active ? officeNow : null
  const partial = active && result && result.incomplete
  const NP = "not possible (XGBoost)"
  const v = x => o ? x.toFixed(2) : (partial ? NP : "0.00")
  const glmRows = partial ? Object.entries(result.components).map(([name, comp]) =>
      [`${name === "large" ? "Large-claim part (GLM)" : name} (annual)`, comp.cost * result.final / result.as_is, false, true])
      .concat(Object.keys(result.missing_components).map(name => [`${name === "small" ? "Small-claim part (XGBoost)" : name}`, null, false, false])) : []
  const rowsSpec = [
    ...glmRows,
    ["Risk premium (annual)", o ? o.risk_premium : 0, true],
    [PROPERTY_LINES.includes(l) ? `+ Cat reinsurance (${(rates.cat_reinsurance * 100).toFixed(0)}% of risk)` : "+ Cat reinsurance (property only)", o ? o.cat_reinsurance : 0],
    [`+ Fixed expense per policy`, o ? o.fixed_expense : 0],
    [`+ Variable expense (${(rates.variable_expense * 100).toFixed(0)}%)`, o ? o.variable_expense : 0],
    [`+ Commission (${active ? currentCase.channel.replace("_", " ") : "channel"}${o ? `, ${(o.commission_rate * 100).toFixed(0)}%` : ""})`, o ? o.commission : 0],
    [`+ Premium tax (${(rates.premium_tax * 100).toFixed(0)}%)`, o ? o.premium_tax : 0],
    [`+ Profit margin (${(rates.target_profit_margin * 100).toFixed(0)}%)`, o ? o.profit_margin : 0],
    ["= Office premium (annual)", o ? o.office_premium : 0, true],
  ]
  const status = !active ? "Not used for this policy" : (o ? `In use: ${currentCase.row_id}` : `In use: ${currentCase.row_id} (GLM part only, XGBoost part missing)`)
  return html`<div class="calc-panel" style="flex:1; min-width:260px; border:2px solid ${active ? "#1d4ed8" : "#cbd5e1"}; border-radius:10px; padding:12px 14px; ${active ? "" : "opacity:0.45; filter:grayscale(1); background:#f1f5f9;"}">
    <div style="font-weight:700; font-size:1.1rem;">${lineNames[l]} calculator</div>
    <div style="font-size:0.85rem; margin-bottom:8px; color:${active ? "#1d4ed8" : "#64748b"};">${status}</div>
    <table style="width:100%; font-size:0.9rem;">
      ${rowsSpec.map(([label, x, bold, shown]) => html`<tr style="${bold ? "font-weight:700; border-top:1px solid #cbd5e1;" : ""}"><td>${label}</td><td style="text-align:right;">${shown ? x.toFixed(2) : v(x)}</td></tr>`)}
    </table>
    ${active && o ? html`<div style="font-size:0.85rem; margin-top:8px;">For the policy's period (${currentCase.policy.exposure.toFixed(3)} yrs): risk ${(o.risk_premium * currentCase.policy.exposure).toFixed(2)}. Written premium in the file: ${currentCase.written_premium.toFixed(2)} (annual).</div>` : ""}
    ${partial ? html`<div style="font-size:0.85rem; margin-top:8px;">Limitation: the buildings small-claim model is XGBoost, so the risk and office premiums can't be completed here. The GLM large-claim part includes its 2025 trend, Pareto adjustment and level step. Written premium in the file: ${currentCase.written_premium.toFixed(2)} (annual).</div>` : ""}
  </div>`
}
```

```{ojs}
html`<div style="display:flex; gap:14px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin:8px 0 16px;">${["motor", "contents", "buildings"].map(calcPanel)}</div>`
```

```{ojs}
officeNow ? md`**How it's built:** office premium = (risk premium ${PROPERTY_LINES.includes(line) ? "x (1 + cat reinsurance)" : ""} + fixed expense) / (1 - variable expense - commission - premium tax - profit margin) = (${officeNow.risk_premium.toFixed(2)}${PROPERTY_LINES.includes(line) ? ` + ${officeNow.cat_reinsurance.toFixed(2)}` : ""} + ${officeNow.fixed_expense.toFixed(2)}) / (1 - ${officeNow.loading.toFixed(2)}) = **${officeNow.office_premium.toFixed(2)}**. The same formula as Gerard's \`office_premium.py\`; every figure is per policy-year.` : md``
```

Inputs.table(refData.expenses.table.map(d => ({item: d.item.replace(/_/g, " "), emerging: d.emerging === null ? "none given" : d.emerging, developed: d.developed === null ? "none given" : d.developed, unit: d.unit})), {layout: "auto", select: false})

The emerging market is used. It gives no comparison-site commission, so the developed market's 10% stands in
(Gerard's assumption, for the team to confirm); none of the 20 reference policies sells through a comparison site.
Cat reinsurance applies to the property lines (home contents and buildings) only.

```{ojs}
inputs = priced ? model.lines[line].inputs : ({})
```

```{ojs}
function optionLabel(inp, value) {
  const row = inp.options.find(o => o.value === String(value))
  const lab = row ? row.label : String(value)
  return lab === "true" ? "Yes" : lab === "false" ? "No" : lab
}
```

```{ojs}
// A slider with an "Unknown" tick box. Its value is null when Unknown is ticked,
// which the engine prices with the model's own missing-value level.
function rangeWithUnknown(inp, value) {
  const unknown = value === null || value === undefined
  const mid = Math.round(((inp.min + inp.max) / 2) / inp.step) * inp.step
  const range = Inputs.range([inp.min, inp.max], {label: inp.label, value: unknown ? mid : value, step: inp.step})
  const box = Inputs.toggle({label: "Unknown", value: unknown})
  const el = html`<div class="unknown-wrap">${range}${box}</div>`
  const sync = () => {
    el.value = box.value ? null : range.value
    range.querySelectorAll("input").forEach(i => i.disabled = box.value)
  }
  range.addEventListener("input", sync)
  box.addEventListener("input", sync)
  sync()
  return el
}
```

```{ojs}
viewof factors = Inputs.form(
  Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(inputs).map(([key, inp]) => [key,
    inp.type === "select"
      ? Inputs.select(inp.options.map(o => o.value), {label: inp.label, value: String(currentCase.policy[key] ?? inp.default), format: v => optionLabel(inp, v)})
      : inp.allow_missing
        ? rangeWithUnknown(inp, currentCase.policy[key])
        : Inputs.range([inp.min, inp.max], {label: inp.label, value: currentCase.policy[key] ?? inp.min, step: inp.step})
  ])),
  {template: parts => html`<div class="controls-grid">${Object.values(parts)}</div>`}
)
```

```{ojs}
viewof newBusiness = Inputs.toggle({label: "New business", value: Boolean(currentCase.policy.new_business)})
```

```{ojs}
policy = ({...factors, new_business: newBusiness, exposure: 1})
```

```{ojs}
result = priced ? scorePolicy(model, line, policy) : null
```

```{ojs}
original = priced ? scorePolicy(model, line, {...currentCase.policy, exposure: 1}) : null
```

```{ojs}
segmentText = result ? (result.segment === "nb" ? "New business" : "Renewal") : ""
```

```{ojs}
waterfall = {
  const rows = []
  if (!result) return rows
  for (const [name, comp] of Object.entries(result.components)) {
    for (const t of comp.terms) {
      rows.push({component: name, step: `${name}: ${inputs[t.input]?.label ?? t.term}`, delta: t.contribution})
    }
    rows.push({component: name, step: `${name}: 2025 trend`, delta: Math.log(comp.trend_multiplier)})
    if (Math.abs(Math.log(comp.scale)) > 1e-15) rows.push({component: name, step: `${name}: Pareto adjustment`, delta: Math.log(comp.scale)})
  }
  return rows
}
```

```{ojs}
result ? html`<div class='hero-kpis'>
  <div class='kpi-card'><div class='kpi-label'>Segment</div><div class='kpi-value'>${segmentText}</div></div>
  <div class='kpi-card'><div class='kpi-label'>${result.incomplete ? "GLM part only (annual)" : "Annual risk premium"}</div><div class='kpi-value'>${result.final.toFixed(2)}</div></div>
  <div class='kpi-card'><div class='kpi-label'>${result.incomplete ? "Office premium" : `For the period (${currentCase.policy.exposure.toFixed(3)} yrs)`}</div><div class='kpi-value'>${result.incomplete ? "not possible (XGBoost)" : (result.final * currentCase.policy.exposure).toFixed(2)}</div></div>
  <div class='kpi-card'><div class='kpi-label'>Change vs policy</div><div class='kpi-value'>${(result.final - original.final >= 0 ? "+" : "") + (result.final - original.final).toFixed(2)}</div></div>
</div>` : html``
```

## Spline factor view

Some numeric factors follow a smooth curve rather than fixed bands. Pick one to see its curve; the red dot is
the current policy.

```{ojs}
splineTerms = priced ? Object.values(model.lines[line].components).flatMap(c => c.terms.filter(t => t.kind === "spline")) : []
```

```{ojs}
viewof chosenSpline = Inputs.select(splineTerms.map(t => t.term), {label: "Factor", format: x => inputs[x]?.label ?? x})
```

```{ojs}
splineTerm = splineTerms.find(t => t.term === chosenSpline)
```

```{ojs}
splineX = {
  if (!splineTerm) return []
  const step = Math.max(inputs[chosenSpline].step, (splineTerm.grid_max - splineTerm.grid_min) / 400)
  return d3.range(splineTerm.grid_min, splineTerm.grid_max + step / 2, step).map(x => ({x, y: Math.exp(splineValue(splineTerm, x))}))
}
```

```{ojs}
!splineTerm ? md`` : Plot.plot({
  width: 800,
  x: {label: inputs[chosenSpline].label},
  y: {label: "Relativity", grid: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.line(splineX, {x: "x", y: "y"}),
    inputs[chosenSpline].allow_missing
      ? Plot.ruleY([Math.exp(splineTerm.missing)], {stroke: policy[chosenSpline] === null ? "crimson" : "#999", strokeDasharray: "5 4", strokeWidth: policy[chosenSpline] === null ? 2.5 : 1})
      : null,
    inputs[chosenSpline].allow_missing
      ? Plot.text(["Unknown"], {x: splineTerm.grid_max, y: Math.exp(splineTerm.missing), textAnchor: "end", dy: -7, fill: policy[chosenSpline] === null ? "crimson" : "#666"})
      : null,
    policy[chosenSpline] === null
      ? null
      : Plot.dot([{x: policy[chosenSpline], y: Math.exp(splineValue(splineTerm, policy[chosenSpline]))}], {x: "x", y: "y", r: 5, fill: "crimson"})
  ]
})
```

```{ojs}
splineTerm && inputs[chosenSpline].allow_missing
  ? md`The dashed line is what the model charges when this factor is **unknown**. It's a level of its own, not an average: unknown sits at ${(Math.exp(splineTerm.missing) / d3.max(splineX, d => d.y)).toFixed(2)}x to ${(Math.exp(splineTerm.missing) / d3.min(splineX, d => d.y)).toFixed(2)}x of the known values.`
  : md``
```

## All 20 reference policies

Every reference policy with the model's 2025 risk premium and office premium as given (before any changes on
this page), next to the written premium in the file. Pick one in the
**Reference policy** menu at the top to load it into the calculator.

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(
  allCases.map(c => {
    const r = model.lines[c.line] !== undefined ? scorePolicy(model, c.line, {...c.policy, exposure: 1}) : null
    const annual = r && !r.incomplete ? r.final : null
    const glmPart = r && r.incomplete ? r.final : null
    const o = annual === null ? null : officePremium(annual, c.line, c.channel, rates)
    return {idx: c.idx, type: c.type, row_id: c.row_id, policy_id: c.policy_id, line: lineNames[c.line], channel: c.channel, new_business: c.policy.new_business ? "Yes" : "No",
            period: c.period, exposure: c.policy.exposure.toFixed(3),
            risk_premium_annual: annual === null ? "not possible (XGBoost)" : annual.toFixed(2),
            office_premium_annual: o === null ? "not possible (XGBoost)" : o.office_premium.toFixed(2),
            glm_large_part_annual: glmPart === null ? "" : glmPart.toFixed(2),
            written_premium: c.written_premium.toFixed(2),
            risk_premium_for_period: annual === null ? "not possible (XGBoost)" : (annual * c.policy.exposure).toFixed(2)}
  }),
  {rows: 20, layout: "auto", select: false}
)
```

## How to read this page

* Start with one of the 20 reference policies. Its values load into the rating factors.
* Change one factor at a time to see how the premium moves.
* The table above shows the **relativity** for each factor: values above 1 raise the premium, values below 1 lower it.
* For motor, the final price is the sum of a **small-claim GLM** and a **large-claim GLM**, followed by Gerard's segment-level adjustments.
